dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Anita. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, hello? I have a shed in my backyard, and I'm, like, thinking of moving it? And I don't totally understand if that means I need a permit or not?
Okay, happy to help sort that out. So it's an existing shed, and you want to move it to a different spot on your property. Is that right?
Right, right. It's already there, I'm not buying a new one. I just want it over by the back corner instead of, um, next to the house.
Got it. Can you tell me roughly how big the shed is? Length and width, if you know.
Oh gosh. It's, like, eight by ten? Or maybe ten by ten? I'd have to go out and measure. Is that important?

It can be, yes. Size and the distance from your property lines both matter for sheds. Moving one can count the same as putting one up, because the new location has to meet the setback rules. So you may well need a permit, but the inspector would confirm once they see the details.
Wait, so it's a permit for moving it? I thought a permit was only for building something new?
A lot of people think that. But the question is really where it ends up sitting, not just whether it's new. What's the address?
It's 8 Bridge Street. Down the Point.
Thank you. And is the shed on a foundation or a slab, or does it just sit on the ground, on blocks or something like that?
Just on the ground. On some, like, cinder blocks? I think four of them? Or six.

That's fine, that helps. So for the application, what you'd want to bring is a site plan or a sketch of your lot showing where the shed is now and where you want to put it, with the distances to the property lines. Also the shed dimensions, and any survey or plot plan you have for the property.
Okay, wait, let me grab a pen. Site plan... sketch of the lot. Does it have to be, like, professional? Because I draw terribly?
No, a neat hand sketch with measurements is usually fine. If you have the plot plan from when you bought the house, that's even better, and you can just mark it up.
Oh, I think I have that in a folder somewhere. So the plot plan, the sketch, the size of the shed. Anything else? Like a form? Do I fill out the form here or at home?
You can pick up the application at our counter at City Hall, or you can ask for it and fill it out ahead of time. Bring the sketch, the dimensions, and a photo of the shed wouldn't hurt either.
A photo, okay. Totally. Sorry, I'm writing this down. My daughter says I should just move it and not tell anybody, but that seems wrong?
Better to check first, definitely. If it's too close to a line, you could be asked to move it again.

Ugh, no thanks. Okay. And then I go to City Hall, when? Is it open now? Because I'm, um, planning to go out toward Portsmouth later, there's a diner I like out there that does breakfast all day, and I'm kind of hungry already.
We're open until the end of the afternoon today, so you could stop by, but the counter staff can walk you through the paperwork anytime during the day. Weekdays are best.
Okay, so I bring the plot plan, the sketch, the measurements, and a photo. And that tells me if I need the permit, or do I already need it?
Most likely you'll need one, but the inspector reviews it and tells you for sure. Bringing those things lets them decide on the spot or tell you what's missing.
Okay. I think I'm still a little fuzzy, but I'll go and ask them. Thank you so much.
You're welcome. Call back if anything else comes up. Take care.
You too, bye.
